item.title: 29-year-old Nigerian man killed as tree crushes car in London
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 29-year-old Nigerian man, James Abiwon, has died after a tree fell on his car during Storm Boelo in Mill Hill, north London. According to Metro UK, Abiwon was driving along Dollis Road at about 12.30pm on Sunday when the tree came down in strong winds. Emergency crews, including police officers, firefighters, paramedics and an air ambulance, responded, but he was pronounced dead at the scene. His cousin, Tyrrell Okolo, described him as “a master of everything” and a devoted family man. Abiwon was a tech sales executive who had earned a degree from the University of Essex. He was also a semi-professional footballer with Aldershot, a musician with about 40,000 YouTube viewers and a mentor to many, his cousin said. Abiwon had been preparing to celebrate his 30th birthday with a padel tournament. The event will now go ahead in his memory, with proceeds going to support his family. His close friend, Kwame Affum, 29, said the two had played padel together just two days before the crash. “I’m trying hard to get my head around this,” he told Metro UK. A friend had messaged Abiwon shortly before the accident about money they owed him for the court, but he did not reply, prompting concern. Affum said Abiwon loved sport, was a good footballer and supported Arsenal. He had earned a first-class university degree and recently won an award at work. “He was full of energy and talent,” Affum said. “He was going to celebrate his 30th birthday in two weeks. It just seems impossible this has happened.” A witness who laid flowers at the scene told Metro UK that she heard a helicopter and went outside to find the fallen tree covering the road, with the car trapped beneath it. Abiwon’s girlfriend and best friend arrived while rescuers were still at the scene. The witness said they were shaking as they waited and hoped he would be brought out. The witness said Abiwon’s aunties and other relatives arrived later and were inconsolable. She described him as clearly well loved and said the community had lost one of its own. Traffic on Dollis Road was reportedly heavy at the time, as roadworks on a nearby street had diverted more vehicles onto the route. A neighbour whose home overlooks the scene said: “If it had been 10 minutes later, it could have been me.” The Metropolitan Police said officers were called to Dollis Road at about 12.40pm on Sunday after reports that a tree had fallen onto a moving car. Police are working with the local authority and coroner to establish the circumstances surrounding Abiwon’s death. Storm Boelo brought gusts of up to 84mph across parts of the UK over the weekend. A 60-year-old man was also killed by a falling tree in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, while others were injured. item.title: Flamingos’ World Cup Form Offers Hope For Super Falcons’ Future
item.description: Nigeria’s impressive run at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco is offering hope for the future of the Super Falcons as the senior team faces the challenge of transitioning from an established generation to a new crop of players. The Flamingos have reached the quarter-finals after recovering from an opening 2-1 defeat to Poland, beating Puerto Rico 2-0 and defending champions North Korea 3-1 before overcoming Mexico 2-1 in the Round of 16 on Thursday. Goals from Oluebube Umejiaku and Mary Dunstan secured the victory over Mexico, sending Nigeria into a quarter-final clash against Venezuela on Sunday, November 1. Mary Dunstan celebrates her goal for Flamingos against Mexico. X/@FIFAWWC Beyond their pursuit of a World Cup title, the Flamingos’ performances have offered a glimpse of what Nigeria’s next generation could bring to the senior women’s team. A Generation Showing Promise The need to prepare new players has become increasingly important for the Super Falcons following the departure of experienced internationals. Nigeria’s failure to defend its Women’s Africa Cup of Nations title in 2026 has also renewed attention on the team’s future. Youth teams are designed partly to prepare players for senior international football, but the transition is rarely straightforward. Excelling at U-17 level does not guarantee success against older, more experienced opponents. For Nigeria, therefore, the Flamingos’ progress represents an encouraging starting point rather than a guarantee of future success. Flamingos. Photo credit: FIFA Their response to adversity has been particularly noteworthy. After losing to Poland, they bounced back against Puerto Rico before producing one of their biggest statements of the tournament by defeating North Korea, a two-time champion. According to FIFA records, North Korea had gone 2,900 days without a defeat in regulation time at the U-17 Women’s World Cup. Its last such loss came against Germany on November 14, 2018, when it was beaten 4-1. Nigeria ended that run with a commanding 3-1 victory. Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, Umejiaku and Kanyinsola Rodiat Yusuf scored for the Flamingos, while North Korea managed a late consolation from the penalty spot. The result demonstrated Nigeria’s ability to compete against established youth teams. Their subsequent victory over Mexico has reinforced that impression, although the quarter-final against Venezuela will provide another test. Players To Watch Captain Harmony Chidi leads a squad that has produced several encouraging performances. In attack, Adegbuyi and Umejiaku have scored important goals, with Umejiaku also finding the net against Mexico. Yusuf has contributed creatively and scored a free-kick against North Korea, while Dunstan has also made her mark with goals in the tournament. Tosin Rafiu has contributed to the team’s attacking play, while defenders Azeezat Oduntan, Ohunene Sunday and Esther Stephen have featured in Nigeria’s efforts to contain opponents. item.title: ‘I was warned not to buy car or house’ — Nigerian Pastor recounts ritual wealth
item.description: Pastor Joel Olasunkanmi, an Ogbomoso based cleric, has recounted how his pursuit of wealth through ritual practices allegedly led to a life changing car accident that resulted in the amputation of his leg. Olasunkanmi shared his experience during an interview with BBC Yoruba, saying he turned to a ritualist while pursuing what he described as vain and worldly things. According to the pastor, his involvement in the practice lasted about five years, during which he was instructed to find a young woman he deeply loved and carry out a ritual involving her. “Thirty years ago, I took some steps that made God angry. It was while I was searching for vain and worldly things that I became disabled. I had a car accident on May 26, 2001,” he said. Recounting the instructions given to him by the ritualist, Olasunkanmi alleged that he was asked to find a woman he loved, have sexual intercourse with her and use a white handkerchief to wipe her private parts before presenting it to the ritualist. “The ritualist I sought told me to look for a young lady that I so much loved. I searched for her, had sex with her and used a white handkerchief to wipe her genitals. I took it to the man,” he recounted. He said the ritual eventually brought him wealth, although he claimed he did not fully understand how it happened. However, he alleged that the ritualist placed restrictions on how he could spend the money. “I did become rich. I did not know how it happened. But I did become rich. But I was told I could not buy a car or house from it,” he said. The pastor further disclosed that the vehicle involved in the accident that eventually led to the amputation of his leg was indirectly connected to him because he had provided the money used to purchase it for another person. “At the end of the day, the car that hit me was indirectly mine because I was the one who bought it for him. At the end of the day, my leg was amputated,” he said. Reflecting on his experience, Olasunkanmi urged young Nigerians to exercise patience and avoid seeking quick wealth through questionable means. “I implore the youths of today to be patient in everything they do,” he advised. item.title: Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez targets early return from injury
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is targeting a return from injury earlier than expected after making progress in his recovery from a broken jaw, according to Sky Sports. The Argentina international underwent surgery after sustaining the injury during Chelsea’s visit to Everton earlier this month and had initially indicated that he would be “back in a few weeks”. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso also provided a similar recovery timeframe last week. However, Sky Sports News’ James Savundra reports that there is growing optimism that Martinez could return sooner than anticipated after consulting a specialist about having a protective mask fitted. Chelsea face Manchester United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday before travelling to Sunderland ahead of the upcoming international break. Martinez’s earlier return would be a boost for Alonso, who has relied on 21-year-old Mike Penders in the Argentine’s absence. Penders, who deputised for the former Aston Villa goalkeeper, endured a difficult outing in his first Premier League start against Tottenham last week, scoring an own goal. Martinez was immediately established as Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper following his summer move from Aston Villa. Meanwhile, Chelsea could face another defensive setback after Maxence Lacroix sustained a hamstring injury during their trip to Anfield on Wednesday. The defender was forced off before half-time, adding to Alonso’s growing injury concerns, although the Chelsea manager admitted that it was too early to determine the severity of the problem. “It’s too early to tell how serious it is,” Alonso said. “Unfortunately he felt something in his hamstring and we need a couple of days to check what the injury’s going to be.” Chelsea are already without Joao Pedro, Reece James, Martinez, Pep Chavarria and Jamie Gittens, while Moises Caicedo and Malo Gusto have also been dealing with minor fitness issues. Despite their injury problems, Morgan Rogers believes Chelsea showed character in their response to last weekend’s defeat to Tottenham, following their performance against Liverpool at Anfield. “To show that reaction shows we have players in the dressing room with character and fight – that’s all you can ask,” he said. “Of course we will get better tactically and technically in terms of the way we want to play. “We showed real fight after that loss and to put in a performance against a tough team, I’m proud of the boys and now we have to keep moving forward.” Vanguard News The post Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez targets early return from injury appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Badenoch condemns racist attacks after ‘Nigerian scammer’ remark
item.description: British Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has condemned what she described as racist attacks against her after a former aide to Reform UK leader Nigel Farage called her a “Nigerian scammer”. Badenoch accused Reform UK politicians of exploiting her Nigerian background for political advantage, insisting that attempts to use her race against her would not succeed. She spoke during an interview on ITV’s Good Morning Britain on Thursday, following a series of social media posts by Raheem Kassam, a former senior aide to Farage. Kassam, who previously served as editor-in-chief of Breitbart News, described Badenoch as an “unrelenting scammer”. In another post, he wrote, “How are people still falling for this Nigerian scammer? Don’t give her your credit card number and bank account details!” Reacting to the comments, Badenoch said, “I think it just shows the sort of people they are.” “I think they think that maybe using my race is a way for them to improve their standing. “Britain is not a racist country, and because it’s not a racist country, their racist attacks and using my race as an attack form is not going to work,” she said. The controversy also drew attention to the response of Reform UK’s Treasury spokesman, Robert Jenrick, who declined to condemn Kassam’s comments. Asked during an ITV interview whether he considered the remarks racist, Jenrick said he did not, although he acknowledged that they could be unpleasant or rude. “It’s not my place to police everybody’s tweets who may or may not be a supporter of Reform,” he said. Farage had also faced questions over whether he considered Kassam’s comments racist during an appearance on BBC Breakfast earlier in the week. “I don’t think saying somebody grew up in Nigeria is racist,” he said. Following further questioning, Farage acknowledged that the comment was excessive but maintained that it was not deliberately racist. “Do I think the comment was over the top? Yes, I do. Do I think it was intentionally racist? No, I don’t,” he added. The post Badenoch condemns racist attacks after ‘Nigerian scammer’ remark appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu prays for Nigeria’s peace, security at lesser Hajj
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described his Umrah pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia as spiritually fulfilling, saying he used the opportunity to pray for Nigeria. The president spoke with journalists shortly after performing the lesser Hajj in Makkah on Friday in an interview shared online by the Nigerian Television Authority. Asked what the spiritual exercise meant to him, particularly given his previous visit to Saudi Arabia ahead of the 2023 presidential election, Tinubu said it gave him a sense of fulfilment. “I feel good, I feel fulfilled, gives me a sense of spiritual thing for me, and the country, and the children,” he said. “I believe the love of the people, the commitment to the job, and the visible commitment to our Allah’s wish, Inshallah, and there’s no other God but Allah,” Tinubu added. The President said he prayed for peace, harmony and happiness among Nigerians, urging the need for continued faith in God. In a separate statement on Friday, his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, disclosed that Tinubu performed the Umrah early in the morning at the Grand Mosque, Masjid al-Haram. Onanuga said the president offered prayers of thanksgiving and sought Allah’s continued guidance and protection for Nigeria. He added that Tinubu prayed for national unity, lasting peace and stability, as well as an end to insecurity and other challenges confronting the country. The president also expressed optimism about Nigeria’s economic and social development, reiterating his administration’s commitment to building a peaceful and prosperous nation. item.title: INEC blames registration officers for AI-generated photos in voters’ register
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has blamed some of its registration officers for introducing suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other irregularities into the preliminary register of voters. INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, disclosed this on Friday during an interview on Arise Television, saying some registration officers used their login details to introduce questionable records into the commission’s database. Bayode said the irregularities were discovered through the commission’s Automated Biometric Identification System, which was deployed to examine the registration records. “We have registration officers on the field. And these registration officers, they have login details to log into the system. “So what we have found is that some of these registration officers, not all of them now, some of them across the states nationwide, they’ve done different things to bring these irregularities onto the register,” he said. He explained that while some of the photographs were generated using artificial intelligence, others were products of poor registration procedures. “Some of these pictures are AI-generated. Some of them not AI-generated, but very bad registration. And this thing got into the register by the registration officers because they have access to register people,” Bayode said. The ICT director added that the commission had identified the questionable records and established how some of the irregularities occurred, but could not determine the reasons behind the actions of the officers involved. “When the ABIS was run on the system, we saw these people. We know what they did. We know how they did it. But honestly, I don’t know why,” he added. Bayode said INEC had begun cleaning up the register before publishing its preliminary version, noting that the commission was working within the statutory 90-day period for the exercise. The disclosure comes amid public concerns over suspicious photographs and other anomalies in the preliminary register uploaded to INEC’s website on October 26. Screenshots circulated on social media had shown photographs suspected to be AI-generated attached to voter records in parts of Edo State. Other concerns included alleged duplicate entries and complaints by some registered voters that their details were missing from the online register. item.title: Obi’s 2027 economic plan targets N500/$1, says Utomi
item.description: Political economist and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Pat Utomi, says the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, plans to strengthen the naira to N500 per dollar if elected in 2027. In a post on X on Thursday, he said the plan to strengthen the naira from its current level of about N1,350 to N500 per dollar would help control inflation, reduce poverty and boost Nigerians’ purchasing power. “We are convinced that targeting a strategic appreciation of the exchange rate by reasonably strengthening it from ₦1,350/$ to ₦500/$ as part of our manifesto is a winning strategy,” he wrote. “It offers a direct, multi-faceted approach to curbing inflation, reducing poverty, and lowering the cost of living.” He projected that a loaf of sliced bread currently selling for N1,750 could fall to N800, while the price of a 50kg bag of imported rice could drop from N55,000 to N27,500. Also, a medium-sized tuber of yam would decline from N2,400 to N1,200, while a 50kg bag of maize could fall from N75,000 to N37,500. Utomi further projected that a bunch of plantain would drop from N2,500 to N1,250, while the price of whole chicken could fall from N7,000 to N3,500. A dozen eggs could sell for N1,150, down from N2,300, while a painter of garri could decline from N1,300 to N650. Utomi said the proposal reflected the party’s commitment to improving living conditions, particularly for Nigerians experiencing multidimensional poverty. “It clearly demonstrates our concrete plan to uplift the 140 million Nigerians currently experiencing multi-dimensional poverty,” he added. The post Obi’s 2027 economic plan targets N500/$1, says Utomi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Alli faults Makinde over doctors’, lecturers’ strikes, promises workers better welfare
item.description: The All Progressives Congress governorship candidate in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Alli, has promised prompt payment of salaries, allowances and other entitlements to workers if elected in the 2027 governorship election. Alli also criticised Governor Seyi Makinde over the ongoing strikes by medical and dental officers in the state and lecturers at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Ogbomoso, accusing him of neglecting the welfare of workers and residents. The APC candidate made his position known in a statement issued on Thursday by the Director of Media and Publicity of the Sharafadeen Alli Campaign Organisation, Bisi Oladele, in Ibadan. The medical workers began their strike on Monday, while members of the LAUTECH branch of the Academic Staff Union of Universities embarked on an indefinite strike on Thursday. The campaign organisation said the industrial actions had disrupted healthcare and education services, leaving patients in public hospitals without access to essential medical attention. It faulted the state government for allowing disputes over outstanding allowances and the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement to escalate into strikes. The organisation also described the demands of the medical workers as legitimate, noting that they included payment of outstanding allowances and restoration of salaries for personnel transferred from field assignments to the Ministry of Health. It warned that the withdrawal of medical services would worsen the challenges facing public hospitals, particularly for vulnerable residents who depend on government healthcare facilities. “Every additional day of this strike raises serious concerns about access to emergency treatment, continuity of care and the welfare of vulnerable patients,” the statement said. The campaign organisation also accused Makinde of prioritising his presidential ambition over the crises in the state. “Rather than remain at his duty post to resolve a crisis that has further crippled an already struggling public healthcare and education system, the governor is busy chasing the mirage of an illusory presidential ambition,” it said. It added that “the allure of presidential power appears to have eclipsed the solemn obligations of his present office.” The organisation appealed to the striking workers to remain open to dialogue and urged the state government to make emergency arrangements to protect patients requiring urgent medical attention. It said an Alli-led administration would prioritise workers’ welfare, constructive engagement with health professionals and the provision of modern equipment and facilities in public hospitals. item.description: …. As G100 holds second summit Nov. 9 By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Roman Catholic Cardinal John Onaiyekan has thrown his weight behind efforts by opposition parties under the G100 Coalition to present a united front ahead of the 2027 elections, as the Coalition prepares to hold its second summit on Monday, November 9, 2026. The leaders of the Coalition, comprising National Chairmen and National Secretaries of some political parties, briefed the Cardinal at his residence on Thursday in Abuja. In a statement signed on behalf of the Coalition Parties, Salihu Moh. Lukman said the leaders told His Eminence about “initiatives and efforts being made to present a united front of opposition political parties and ensure that Nigerians are presented with a credible alternative to rescue the country.” Among those who met the cardinal were the factional national chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Alhaji Kabiru Tanimu Turaki SAN, and the faction’s national secretary, Honourable Daniel Woyengikuro. The Social Democratic Party SDP National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Umar Abubakar Gombe, and the People’s Redemption Party PRP National Chairman, Dr Hakeem Baba Ahmed, were also there, alongside the PRP National Secretary, Mr Sunny Kanu. Professor Jibrin Ibrahim, a civil society activist and scholar, facilitated the meeting. The Cardinal was told that work had been concluded on three working papers of the Coalition. They are “The National Covenant for Democratic Renewal, which outlined the principles of the Coalition; The Framework for Opposition Unity, which describes how the coalition will work; and The National Reform Programme, which sets out what a government built on this cooperation would seek to do for Nigerians.” According to the statement, Coalition leaders are working to conclude and adopt the papers before the Second Summit on November 9, where all the political parties under the Coalition will endorse and unveil them. The Cardinal expressed support for the efforts of opposition parties and their candidates to unite, with the aim of building “a robust opposition which is vital to the sustenance of Nigeria’s democratic traditions”. He also expressed joy that Nigerians “will have real and credible choices to enable citizens to decide their future and leaders next year.” His Eminence further stressed “the role of competent, honest and sympathetic leaders in resolving the multiple problems which combine to make the decent lives of our citizens difficult or impossible to sustain.” The delegation reported “the successes registered in attracting more parties to join the Coalition and designing mechanisms that should resolve potential sources of discord.” It also thanked the Cardinal for his “lifelong stand for justice and compassion” and asked him to continue to pray for the success of the Coalition. item.title: Netanyahu bloc finishes ahead in Israel vote, but well short of majority
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a majority, final results from Israel’s general election showed Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote. Netanyahu’s coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, with his Likud party remaining the largest faction with 27 seats. The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot, secured 48 seats. The results from the Central Elections Committee also cemented the emergence as potential kingmakers of the Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List, with the two winning a combined 19 seats. The fragmented outcome sets the stage for difficult negotiations to form a government that could last weeks, with no single bloc able to reach the 61-seat threshold needed and the prospect of another election remaining if talks fail. The final tally came after Netanyahu’s camp spent Thursday amplifying unproven allegations that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding to influence the vote, accusations rejected by both Arab-majority lists and Qatar. Israel’s Shin Bet domestic security service said it was investigating suspected irregularities, but stressed the probe was not intended to “cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote in a democratic and lawful manner”. The electoral commission also sought to calm tensions, with its acting director general Dean Livne saying any suggestion of widespread issues was “entirely groundless”. – Political earthquake – The controversy centred on allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas, to finance vote-buying operations. “The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party said on Thursday. Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing and welcomed an investigation, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu and his allies of conducting a “campaign of incitement” out of fear of Arab voters’ growing political influence. Government officials have so far provided no evidence to back the allegations. Opposition figures accused Netanyahu of attempting to undermine confidence in the results after failing to secure a governing majority. “He is trying to challenge the election results,” left-wing candidate Yair Golan said. Eisenkot said he was briefed by the Shin Bet and the election committee, adding it was “too early to understand what happened, and whether anything happened at all”. But he continued: “It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election.” Netanyahu himself has long been under the cloud of allegations related to Qatar after the arrests last year of two of his aides for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf state. item.title: Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi affirms court acquittal in sworn affidavit
item.description: A Lagos-based businessman, Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi, has confirmed that he and his company, Kenten Table Water Nigeria Limited, were discharged and acquitted by the Federal High Court sitting in Umuahia, Abia State. Nwaobasi made the affirmation in an affidavit sworn before a Notary Public of Nigeria in Satellite Town, Lagos. Nwaobasi and his company had been charged in a five-count amended charge filed on November 21, 2024, involving allegations of conspiracy to possess hard drugs and money laundering. In an affidavit of facts dated August 4, 2026, and made available to journalists, Nwaobasi identified himself as the first defendant in Charge No. FHC/UM/CR/143/2024, between the Federal Republic of Nigeria and Nwaobasi Kelechi Monday (also known as Nwaobasi Kelechi Michael, “Aboy”) and Kenten Table Water Nigeria Limited. He stated that, on May 29, 2025, the Federal High Court sitting in Umuahia, Abia State, discharged and acquitted him and his company, the second defendant in the case. According to him, the order was made by the Federal High Court, Umuahia, presided over by Honourable Justice K. O. Ogundare. He explained that the affidavit was required for official and record purposes. “I swear to this affidavit in good faith, believing same to be true and correct to the best of my knowledge in accordance with the Oaths Law of Lagos State 2015,” Nwaobasi stated. In its ruling, the court held that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Nwaobasi and his company on any of the five counts. The judge found that the evidence presented by the prosecution was insufficient to warrant calling on the defendants to enter their defence to the charges. “In sum, I find that no prima facie case has been made out against the defendants by the prosecution in all the counts as the prosecution has failed to prove the elements of the offence in each of the counts. “Consequently, the no case submission is hereby upheld and the defendants are hereby discharged and acquitted on each of the 1st -5th counts of the offence charged by virtue of Section 357 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015,” the judge held in a ruling delivered in open court. The certified true copy of the ruling made available to journalists listed E. C. Onyema-Opara, Esq., as counsel for the prosecution, while V. A. Ekwegh, Esq., and O. E. Porbeni, Esq., were listed as counsel for the defendants. The post Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi affirms court acquittal in sworn affidavit appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Adamu makes history as first Nigerian CAF General Secretary
item.description: Nigerian football administrator Samson Adamu has been confirmed as the substantive General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), becoming the first Nigerian to occupy the position in the organisation’s 70-year history. The confirmation was announced on Thursday, with the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) congratulating Adamu on his appointment. The NFF’s acting general secretary, Emmanuel Ikpeme, described the development as a significant moment for Nigerian football administration and expressed confidence in Adamu’s ability to excel in the role. “This is, indeed, very good news. I am so happy for Samson Adamu on his confirmation, and I know he is going to make Nigeria and Africa proud,” Ikpeme said. “The NFF is delighted with this appointment, and we will give him all the necessary support as a member association under CAF. We wish him tremendous success in the job,” Ikpeme added. Adamu joined CAF, the continent’s football governing body headquartered in Cairo, Egypt, as Director of Competitions before becoming Director of Tournaments and Events. He was appointed acting general secretary on March 29 following the resignation of his predecessor, Veron Mosengo-Omba, a Swiss-Congolese football administrator. Adamu holds a FIFA Master’s degree in the management, law and humanities of sport. He began his career in football administration by establishing the now-defunct Copa Lagos beach soccer tournament in the early 2010s. item.title: Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen
item.description: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that had resulted in the freezing of more than $2.5 billion in an effort to prevent them from being stolen. The company — the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes — said it had suspended trading on certain products. It nevertheless insisted: “User funds are completely safe.” Several experts said it looked like a massive amount of assets had been stolen. “It does look like a hack on Binance,” said former Binance chief Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the group but remains a majority shareholder. Paolo Ardoino, the CEO of Tether — a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT — said his firm froze about $1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Circle boss Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC. USDT and USDC are both “stablecoins,” or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar. For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform. Some said it could be the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind, with a haul exceeding the $1.5 billion stolen in February 2025 from the Bybit platform — an incident attributed to hackers affiliated with North Korea. Bitcoin prices fell more than three percent on the news. The post Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: AFCON to hold every two years again as CAF reverses decision
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-year cycle. The decision was unanimously approved by the CAF Executive Committee, with President Patrice Motsepe announcing the development after the organisation’s Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026. The reversal comes after CAF reviewed its earlier plan to move AFCON to a four-year schedule and introduce an Africa Nations League as a biennial competition. CAF said the proposed Nations League would take several years to generate the financial resources and football development benefits required to make its competitions globally competitive and financially sustainable. In a statement published on its website on Thursday, Motsepe said the decision to retain the two-year AFCON cycle was taken in the interest of African football, the confederation’s 54 member associations and African players playing for clubs outside the continent. “The decision by the CAF EXCO that the CAF AFCON should take place every Two Years was based on advancing, protecting and promoting the interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations, as well as the interest of African players employed by Football Clubs outside Africa,” he said. Motsepe added that CAF was concerned about the time it would take for the proposed Africa Nations League to deliver the financial and developmental gains initially expected from the competition. He said the new tournament was intended to mirror the existing AFCON format and take place every two years, but would not provide the required support for African football in the immediate future. Under the revised calendar, the next AFCON will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament. The subsequent editions are scheduled for 2028, 2031 and 2033, with CAF maintaining that the competition will not be staged in a FIFA World Cup year. Motsepe expressed confidence in the three East African countries’ ability to deliver a successful tournament in 2027. He also described AFCON as more than a football competition, saying it provides an opportunity to celebrate Africa’s cultures and bring people from across the continent and the diaspora together. “The AFCON competition is also about celebrating African Football and Africa’s rich and diverse cultures, customs and traditions and bringing people together from Africa’s 54 Countries, the African Diaspora and throughout the world,” he said. “The CAF EXCO decision is in the best interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations and will also contribute significantly to the development and growth of football in Africa,” he added. item.title: Gunmen kill four in Plateau community
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Four persons were reportedly killed when gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night. The attackers were said to have stormed the community at about 8pm and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to check attacks and restore security. A resident of Barkin Ladi, Mr Bulus Jok, who confirmed the incident, said, “The gunmen struck the community around 8pm despite the curfew in place and started shooting sporadically.” Jok said, “They were shooting at anything they saw. The attack created panic in the community, and four people were killed.” He added, “The incident is very sad, especially as there had been an early warning alert sent to the relevant authorities a day before the attack.” Also confirming the incident, Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, Mr Rwang Tengwong, said, “Terrorist gangs reportedly attacked Sabon Angwa, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area, and shot four people dead.” Tengwong condemned the attack, describing the killing of innocent residents as unacceptable, adding, “We condemn this latest attack in strong terms and lament the loss of these lives.” He said, “It is disturbing that communities are still being attacked despite the security measures and curfew put in place to protect residents.” The BYM spokesman urged security operatives to intensify surveillance and take proactive measures to prevent further attacks on vulnerable communities, saying, “We call on security agencies to strengthen their presence and respond promptly to early warning alerts.” Efforts to reach security operatives for more details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 30, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira opened today, Friday, October 30, 2026, holding firm against the United States Dollar across both the official foreign exchange window and the parallel market, following sustained liquidity interventions by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and healthy diaspora inflows. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the spot exchange rate traded at N1,346.86 per dollar during early morning transactions. Commercial banks and corporate importers observed orderly liquidity conditions as FX demand for trade obligations, tuition fees, and capital repatriation continued to be met across authorized channels. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, street traders and Bureau De Change operators across major economic centers, including Lagos, Abuja, and Kano, quoted buying rates around N1,375 per dollar, while selling rates hovered around N1,385 per dollar. The price gap between the official market and the parallel window remains narrow. Financial analysts attribute the relative stability of the local currency to Nigeria’s solid foreign reserve buffer, which remains well above $55 billion, enabling the central bank to cushion short-term demand shocks and maintain stability across trading channels. Market experts expect trading to remain steady throughout the business day as routine demand is steadily absorbed by market liquidity. item.title: 2027: Pantami, Gwarzo in, Adebutu out
item.description: After more than two weeks of suspense, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) yesterday took a final decision on the fate of candidates nominated by political parties for governorship and House of Assembly seats who were not initially cleared by the commission. The commission’s top officials, after series of meetings with its chairman, Prof Joash Amupitan, cleared former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Ali Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The electoral commission, however, rejected a petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list of candidates. INEC explained that the right of those cleared to contest is subject to the outcomes of pending court cases against them. The commission, however, gave a window of 14 days to those omitted to forward their petitions to the commission for possible review. Our correspondents report that after the close of submission on the 24th, in which all the affected filed their petitions, INEC promised to come up with a final decision on the petitions on the 29th. And after a meeting which lasted for over six hours on Thursday, it declared that some of the candidates have been cleared. A competent source at INEC, who spoke to Daily Trust after the commission’s meeting on Thursday, said the commission received 69 petitions from political parties concerning omitted candidates for governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections. The source said about 36 petitions were successful, while the others failed. “We received a total of 69 petitions from political parties. Some of the successful ones, I think about 36, and the rest didn’t succeed,” the source said. The source, however, said the commission was still awaiting the final figures from its legal department. On Pantami and Gwarzo, the source said the commission had no objection to their candidacy, but noted that the pending court cases could affect their eligibility. “Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP candidate in Gombe State. item.title: Gunmen kill police inspector, 11 others in Kebbi
item.description: Residents of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi in Besse/Shanga riverine areas of Kebbi State have fled their communities as suspected members of the Lakurawa and Mamudawa terror groups killed 11 residents and a police inspector in a series of attacks they have launched on the communities. The terrorists carried out a series of attacks on the communities in Besse and Shanga from the 22nd to 28 October, this year, Daily Trust gathered. During the attacks, they burnt houses and looted property as they moved along the River Niger bank from Kaoje to Besse. A local who spoke to our corespondent, Aminu Usman, said the attack on the communities was devastating as the gunmen burnt houses and property before retreating to their hideouts. He said, “the attack took many of the villagers unawares. No one expected that the Lakurawa terrorists would attack us. The attack was carried out in a coordinated manner. They burnt our houses and looted our property. Many people have been rendered homeless and they have fled the communities,” he said. A source said, “They killed people and took their valuables. They burnt motorcycles and broke into shops and took whatever they wanted.” He added that rumour of the attacks triggered the mobilisation of vigilantes known as Yan Sakai, who allegedly attacked some Fulani traders at Samanaji Market on October 22, 2026. A resident who spoke to our correspondent said, “I know a man who lost four of his family members in the attack. As I speak, only a few people are left in the affected communities.
